subject.title: iOS/macOS app cannot connect to a Gateway behind a Basic-auth reverse proxy

question: Should macOS adopt the same per-gateway custom-header contract already landed for iOS and Android, or should its reverse-proxy auth surface be narrower or deferred?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the macOS implementation would persist and send pre-Gateway credentials, so maintainers need to choose the storage, TLS, redaction, reset, and endpoint-scoping boundary before automation implements it.

options.title: Mirror the landed mobile contract
options.body: Add macOS per-gateway custom headers with secure storage, TLS-only gateway attachment, reserved-header filtering, reset behavior, and parity tests matching the iOS/Android contract.

options.title: Limit macOS to typed proxy auth
options.body: Expose only narrower Basic/Bearer-style fields first, reducing arbitrary-header risk but diverging from the mobile custom-header contract.

options.title: Defer macOS proxy credentials
options.body: Keep macOS unsupported for authenticating reverse proxies for now and document direct, VPN, tunnel, or proxy-bypass alternatives.

recommendation.title: Mirror the landed mobile contract
recommendation.body: Add macOS per-gateway custom headers with secure storage, TLS-only gateway attachment, reserved-header filtering, reset behavior, and parity tests matching the iOS/Android contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the landed mobile contract and recent adjacent native Gateway work, making him the best available owner for the security-boundary decision.
